Ba Sing Se and Us
Consider what Ba Sing Se expects of our realm this year.
Withhold Tribute from Ba Sing Se

Ba Sing Se is far away and its demands are many. Stop sending tribute. Where the crown is strong enough to expect it, each year of defiance costs the Earth King authority and angers them, but our standing grows.
Resume Tribute to Ba Sing Se
Make peace with the crown and send tribute again.

A courier in the green and gold of Ba Sing Se has arrived with a sealed command from [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Foreign armies have marched on the Earth Kingdom, and the crown reminds us that realms which owe it obedience are expected to stand with it.
We stand with Ba Sing Se.
This is not our war.
Ba Sing Se is a name we honour and little more. With the crown this weak, or this far away, our realm is answerable to no one but ourselves. We send nothing.
We recognise the Earth King as the head of the Earth Kingdom. Our realm sends a modest gift each year if we are a duke or greater (2, 4 or 8 gold), and otherwise governs itself.

The crown in Ba Sing Se is strong enough to expect tribute from us. Each year we send gold: 4 as a duke, 8 as a king and 16 as an emperor. Counts are spared unless the crown commands obedience. It goes into the treasury of Ba Sing Se, not to the Earth King personally. If our capital lies in the de jure kingdom of another independent Earth king, they collect it on the crown's behalf and gain prestige for it. We may withhold it, but the crown will remember.

Ba Sing Se commands obedience from realms this close to the capital. We pay full tribute (2 gold a year even as a count), and when foreign armies attack the Earth King we will be called to defend the crown. Refusing the call costs prestige and damages Ba Sing Se's authority.
So it is.
Withholds Tribute
Answered the Call of Ba Sing Se
Refused the Call of Ba Sing Se
Defying Ba Sing Se
This ruler refuses to send tribute to the Earth King.
The Treasury of Ba Sing Se
Review the crown's treasury and the projects it is paying for.
Send Relief to the Provinces

Send grain, builders and coin to the realms that owe Ba Sing Se. In Kyoshi's day such policies kept the peace between the states. Their rulers will think better of the crown, and the crown's authority grows.
Proclaim the Mandate of Ba Sing Se
Spend lavishly on ceremony, envoys and gifts to remind the states who wears the crown. Royal Authority increases greatly.
Draw on the Treasury
The treasury belongs to the crown, and we are the crown. Take 100 gold from it. Half of it reaches our purse, the rest disappears along the way, and word of it weakens the crown's authority.

No relief has been sent in the last five years
The Mandate has not been proclaimed in the last ten years
We have not drawn on the treasury in the last two years
Very well.
Reformed Bureaucracy
The crown pays its clerks properly. Paid from the treasury of Ba Sing Se.
Council of Five Funded
The generals of the Council of Five keep a standing force. Paid from the treasury of Ba Sing Se.
Dai Li Funded
The Dai Li watch the court and the city. Paid from the treasury of Ba Sing Se.
Strengthened Border
The crown has paid for a larger garrison and stronger walls here.
Relief from Ba Sing Se
Work: The Royal Messenger Network

Post stations, relays of riders and messenger hawks along every road, day and night. Once finished, Ba Sing Se's word reaches the far states in days instead of months, and the crown's reach grows with it. Costs 20 gold a year to keep running afterwards.
Work: The Royal Roads

Paved roads and granaries across the Earth Kingdom. Once finished, every province of the Earth Kingdom outside the desert can feed larger armies and trades a little more, whoever owns it, invaders included. Costs 15 gold a year to maintain afterwards.
Work: A Single Law for the Kingdom

Every state and town of the Earth Kingdom keeps its own laws. Replace them with one code written in Ba Sing Se. Once finished, tribute rises by half and the crown gains authority, but every state that pays will hate the crown's laws for as long as they stand. Needs the States or Monarchism unity law and a paid bureaucracy.
Work: Raise the Outer Wall

Raise a great outer wall around Ba Sing Se with conscripted labour from the provinces. Once finished, the capital becomes nearly impregnable, but the conscription costs the crown authority and goodwill.
The bureaucracy is being paid (budget programme)
Once finished: realms count as §Gcloser§! to Ba Sing Se (near up to 650 instead of 450, far only beyond 1100 instead of 850), so more realms owe more. Upkeep §R20§! gold a year. Resentment §R+20§!.
Once finished: every Earth Kingdom province outside the Si Wong Desert gains supply limit +2 and tax +5%, whoever owns it. Upkeep §R15§! gold a year. Resentment §R+10§!.
Once finished: tribute +50%, Royal Authority +5. Every tribute payer has §R-10§! opinion of the crown while the law stands. Resentment §R+25§!.

Riders in the green and gold of Ba Sing Se now pass through our lands every day, and every relay station has a royal clerk in it. The crown hears of everything we do within days, and expects more of us for it.
The crown's engineers have paved roads and raised granaries through our lands. Trade comes more easily. So, our generals note, would an army.
A herald from Ba Sing Se has read out a single code of law for the whole Earth Kingdom. The customs and courts our ancestors kept for generations are to give way to the clerks of the capital.
The crown has raised a great wall around Ba Sing Se, built by men taken from every province, ours included. Many did not come home.
Ba Sing Se's word is law.
We were here before the crown's clerks. We will pay no more.
Envoys from neighbouring states have come to us in secret. Ba Sing Se reaches too far, they say, and they have stopped sending tribute. They ask us to do the same.
They are right. We stop paying.
We keep faith with Ba Sing Se.
The treasury could no longer pay the riders and relay stations. The Royal Messenger Network has collapsed, and the far states are far again.
A great loss.
The treasury could no longer pay for repairs. The Royal Roads have fallen into disrepair.
A great loss.
Royal Road
A paved road and granaries built by the crown of Ba Sing Se.
The Outer Wall
Ba Sing Se's great outer wall.
Ba Sing Se's Laws
Budget: Pay the Bureaucracy
Pay the clerks of the Grand Secretariat properly. While funded: tax +10%, building cost -10%, and the treasury loses only 3% a year to graft instead of 10%. Costs 12 gold a year from the treasury.
Budget: Stop Paying the Bureaucracy
Save the treasury 12 gold a year. Graft returns.
Budget: Fund the Council of Five
Give the generals of the Council of Five the means to keep a standing force. While funded: retinue +300, levies +10%, morale +5%. Costs 15 gold a year.
Budget: Stop Funding the Council of Five
Save the treasury 15 gold a year.
Budget: Fund the Dai Li

Give the Dai Li the means to watch the court and the city. While funded: plot power +15%, plot defence +30%, plot discovery +20%, and saboteurs are caught more often. But the Dai Li grow more influential every year they are funded. Costs 10 gold a year.
Budget: Stop Funding the Dai Li
Save the treasury 10 gold a year. The Dai Li's influence will slowly fade.
Budget: Garrison the Borders
Keep larger garrisons in every province on the edge of our realm. While funded: garrison +30%, fort level +1, levy reinforcement +20% there. Costs 15 gold a year.
Budget: Withdraw the Border Garrisons
Save the treasury 15 gold a year.
The programme costs §R12§! gold from the treasury every year until stopped. If the treasury cannot pay, it lapses.
The programme costs §R15§! gold from the treasury every year until stopped. If the treasury cannot pay, it lapses.
The programme costs §R10§! gold from the treasury every year until stopped. If the treasury cannot pay, it lapses.
Work: The Royal Granaries
Expand the Agrarian Zone's granaries. Once finished: tax +10% in the Ba Sing Se region, and grain sent to starving provinces costs the treasury half as much.
Work: Investigate the Dai Li
Appoint trusted officials to look into the Dai Li's affairs, quietly. Once finished, the Dai Li's influence drops by 30. Can be repeated.
Purge the Dai Li
The Dai Li answer to themselves now. Remove their leaders and disband their networks. Their influence falls to nothing, their funding ends, and the crown loses authority for the upheaval.
Once finished: Ba Sing Se region fort level +2, garrison +50%, prestige +100. Royal Authority §R-5§!. Resentment §R+15§!.
Once finished: tax +10% in the Ba Sing Se region, famine relief costs 30 instead of 60.
Once finished: Dai Li influence §G-30§!.

Sabotage the Crown's Works

Ba Sing Se builds to bind us tighter. A few paid hands, a fire in a storehouse, a bridge that gives way: the work can be set back a year. If the Dai Li catch our agents, the Earth King will know who sent them. Costs 25 gold.
We have not sabotaged the crown's works in the last five years
If it works, one of the crown's works loses a year of progress
If our agents are caught, we lose §R30§! prestige and the Earth King will know it was us
Or nothing may come of it
Good.
We need more gold.
A great day for Ba Sing Se.
So be it.

The treasury could not pay for this year's work, and one of the crown's works stands idle. If it stalls three years running, it will be abandoned and everything spent on it lost. The treasury holds §Y[global_atx_treasury.GetValue]§! gold.
Three years without pay: the workers have gone home and one of the crown's works has been abandoned. Everything spent on it is lost.

An envoy from [From.GetTitledFirstName] has made the long journey to Ba Sing Se. The harvest has failed in [From.GetHerHis] lands and the people are starving. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks the crown for grain.

An envoy from [From.GetTitledFirstName] has made the long journey to Ba Sing Se. Daofei roam [From.GetHerHis] lands, burning villages and robbing the roads. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks the crown for soldiers.

An envoy from [From.GetTitledFirstName] has made the long journey to Ba Sing Se. Raiders strike [From.GetHerHis] coasts and borders faster than [From.GetSheHe] can answer. [From.GetSheHeCap] asks the crown for soldiers.
Send grain.
Send soldiers.
Ba Sing Se has its own troubles.
Ba Sing Se answered. Help from the crown has reached us, and our people will remember who sent it.
Ba Sing Se has refused us. The crown takes our tribute and gives nothing back.
Our envoy never came back from Ba Sing Se, and no answer has come. Some say the Dai Li keep bad news from the king. Whatever the reason, the crown has left us to fend for ourselves.
Long live the Earth King.
We will remember this. No more tribute.
So be it.
The treasury could not pay the clerks this year. The bureaucracy programme has lapsed, and graft will return.
The treasury could not pay the generals this year. The Council of Five's standing force has been disbanded.
The treasury could not pay the Dai Li this year. Their funding has lapsed.
The treasury could not pay the border garrisons this year. They have been withdrawn.

The Dai Li have become a power of their own. Reports reach us only after they have read them, appointments go to their friends, and courtiers lower their voices when an agent passes. Ba Sing Se is quieter than ever, and we are no longer sure who rules it.
This cannot go on.
Fire in a storehouse, a collapsed scaffold, stolen tools: someone has sabotaged one of the crown's works, and it has lost a year of progress. Nobody knows who paid for it.
Find them.
Our agents caught saboteurs at one of the crown's works before they could do any harm. Under questioning they named their master: [From.GetTitledFirstName].
[From.GetFirstName] will regret this.

Each year graft takes a tenth of it (3% if the bureaucracy is paid, 5% more if the Dai Li are strong), and budget programmes, works in progress and the upkeep of finished great works are paid out of it. Far realms will ask for help, and every answer costs either gold or authority.

The islands answer to us, and the world beyond them is soft. The last Avatar was merciful where they should have been firm, and that mercy left a door open. Our generals have studied the Earth Kingdom's coasts for years. Its harbours are poorly walled and its lords quarrel with Ba Sing Se and with each other.\n\nOne strike, then another. Who would stop us?

There is no Fire Lord, only a scatter of island lords who each call themselves the heir to one. The last Avatar was merciful where they should have been firm, and in the silence they left, ambition has room to grow.\n\nThe islands could be one nation again, under one ruler. Under us.

Ba Sing Se has lost its grip. Its king's word carries no further than the Outer Wall, and the realms of the Earth Kingdom go their own way. The last Avatar was merciful where they should have been firm, and nobody has stopped anyone in a long time.\n\nThe Earth Kingdom needs a ruler who can hold it together, by force if need be. It needs an Empire.
Seize the moment.
We become the champion of Unchecked Ambition. We may wage special wars of conquest until we are stopped, by defeat, by death or by the Avatar.
Let it pass.
Every Avatar solves one problem and leaves another behind. The elders who found you have told you what your past life could not finish. The world is waiting to see whether you will.
Then I will see to it.
Restless Spirits: the last Avatar neglected the spirits. Each year, spirits trouble four more provinces. The Avatar can calm them.
Daofei Country: the Avatar died young or abandoned their duties. Each year, bandits take hold of four more Earth Kingdom provinces. The Avatar can hunt them down.
A Dangerous Instrument: the last Avatar built institutions that outlived their purpose. The Dai Li grew stronger. The Avatar can rein them in.
Unchecked Ambition: the last Avatar was merciful where they should have been firm. An ambitious ruler may rise to conquer. The Avatar can confront them.
An Iron Peace: the last Avatar imposed peace by force. Earth realms resent Ba Sing Se more. The Avatar can heal the divide.
A champion of Unchecked Ambition is waging their wars.

The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is dead. They spent their life on the quarrels of nations and seldom crossed into the Spirit World. Now the spirits are angry, and nobody is left who knows how to speak to them.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is dead. Their time was too short, or they turned away from it. In the years they could not cover, daofei have taken the roads and the hills of the Earth Kingdom.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is dead. They built well, but what they built does not die with them. The Dai Li, sworn to protect the culture of Ba Sing Se, now answer to fewer people every year.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is dead. They spared those they should have stopped. Ambitious rulers have noticed that the Avatar forgives, and they wonder how far forgiveness goes.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is dead. They kept the peace by breaking those who broke it. The peace held, but the Earth realms remember who bent their knees for them.
Every Avatar leaves something behind.
The spirits are calm again. The Avatar walked between the worlds and listened, and the haunted places have gone quiet.
The daofei are broken. The Avatar has hunted the bandit lords out of the hills, and the roads of the Earth Kingdom are safe to travel again.
The Dai Li have been reined in. The Avatar has seen to it that the agents of Lake Laogai answer to the crown again, and not the other way round.
The champion of ambition has stood down. Whether by the Avatar's words or by the Avatar's strength, their wars of conquest are over.
The old wounds are closing. The Avatar has spoken with the lords who were broken to keep the peace, and the Earth realms resent Ba Sing Se a little less.
The world is a little lighter.
Every Avatar solves one problem and leaves another. These are the burdens the world carries now. Each fades on its own in about fifty years, unless the Avatar lifts it first.
I see.

The Avatar has come to [Root.GetTitledName]. They do not come with an army. They come alone, and they ask for the wars to end.\n\nOur generals say the Avatar is one person. Our advisors remind us what one Avatar has done before.
We will stand down.
The Avatar does not rule here.

[From.GetTitledName] has refused to end their wars. They heard you out and then sent you away.\n\nYou could stand beside the people they attack. The Avatar does not take sides lightly, but there are times when the Avatar has to.
I will fight beside those they attack.
Not yet. I will wait and watch.
Word has come from the Fire Islands. The Fire Lord has turned their eyes to the Earth Kingdom's coasts, and the fleets are gathering. Some say the Avatar should have stopped this long ago.
Word has come from the Fire Islands. One of the island lords has declared that the Fire Nation will be one again, and they mean to unite it by fire.
With Ba Sing Se too weak to hold the Earth Kingdom together, an Earth ruler has taken up the cause of Earth imperialism. They mean to unite the realms by force, and some whisper of an Earth Empire.
Where is the Avatar?
[From.GetTitledName] has proclaimed the Earth Empire from the Royal Palace of Ba Sing Se. The old Earth Kingdom is a memory, and a single ruler means to hold all of it.
An Empire, then.
You crossed into the Spirit World and stayed until the angry spirits would speak with you. It took patience. In the end they listened, and the haunted places of the world have gone quiet.
You spent months in the hills of the Earth Kingdom, tracking bandit lords to their camps and breaking them one by one. The roads are safe again.
You went into Lake Laogai and came out again. The Dai Li now know the Avatar is watching, and they answer to the crown once more.
You went from court to court and listened to every lord who was broken to keep the peace. Words cannot undo what was done, but they can stop it from festering.
You did all you could, and it was not enough. Not this time. People are saying the Avatar is not what they used to be. You will have to try again.
It is done.
Next time.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] has set out for the Spirit World to calm the restless spirits.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] has set out to hunt the daofei who plague the Earth Kingdom.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] has gone to Ba Sing Se to rein in the Dai Li.
The Avatar [From.GetFirstName] is travelling from court to court to heal the old divide between Ba Sing Se and the Earth realms.
Good luck to them.
Calm the Restless Spirits
Cross into the Spirit World and make peace with the spirits the last Avatar neglected. The mission takes six months to a year and can fail.
Hunt the Daofei
Go into the hills of the Earth Kingdom and break the bandit lords. The mission takes six months to a year and can fail.
Rein in the Dai Li
Go to Ba Sing Se and remind the Dai Li whom they serve. The mission takes six months to a year and can fail.
Heal the Divide
Travel from court to court and make amends for the peace the last Avatar imposed. The mission takes six months to a year and can fail.
Confront the Champion of Ambition
Go to this ruler and demand that their wars of conquest end. They may refuse.
The Avatar must rest for two years after a mission.
The Avatar confronted a champion less than five years ago.
The Avatar's Legacy
See which burdens past Avatars have left on the world.
Found the Earth Empire
Ba Sing Se is ours. Proclaim the Earth Empire and rule all the Earth Kingdom as its Great Uniter.

The Avatar has taken our side against an aggressor. Our soldiers fight harder for it.
On the Avatar's Mission
The Avatar is away, trying to lift a burden left by a past life.
The Avatar Doubted
The Avatar's last mission failed, and people have noticed.
